column1: # falsifiers.tsv — THE FALSIFIER REGISTRY that scripts/ci-invariants.sh enforces.
# Each row is a security falsifier the twin-deletion + megaswarm-fix campaign
# relies on. `ci-invariants.sh falsifiers` RUNS every row (not just compiles it)
# and FAILS if any row is missing, #[ignore]'d, does not execute, or is red.

#   test_fn   the exact `#[test] fn` name (the registry asserts `fn <test_fn>` exists)

# The whole run sets DREGG_ALLOW_UNAUDITED_PQ=1 so PQ-touching setups (node, game-board)
# run their unaudited-PQ fallback instead of aborting in setup — it does NOT weaken any

column1: # ── the ENROLLMENT tooth on the verified finalization rule ─────────────────────
# The verified rule FINALIZED 100% of a 4-creator / 3-round lace with 3 enrolled, the unenrolled
# creator's three blocks included, and `VerifiedFinality::admits`' own doc-comment said that could
# not happen. It is registered on BOTH sides deliberately: the `dregg-blocklace` row has NO Lean
# dependency and therefore CANNOT self-skip, so the enrollment property stays enforced on an
# archive-less runner where the `dregg-node` row (which routes through the real `dregg_tau_order`
# export and `demand_lean`-skips without the archive) would report a hollow ok.

column4: ordering::tau finalizes NO block from a creator outside `participants` (the enrollment filter mirroring the verified `BlocklaceFinality.enrolledId`), with the anti-vacuity halves: the adversary IS in the lace at every round AND is acked by honest blocks, and all NINE enrolled blocks still finalize in round-major order

the LIVENESS half at n=3..5: on a lace whose every creator IS a participant the enrollment filter drops NOTHING (the Rust face of `tauOrder_enrolled_eq_unfiltered`) — a safety filter that also drops legitimate blocks would be a liveness bug traded for a safety one

the VERIFIED rule (real lace, real `dregg_blocklace_finalize` export) refuses an UNENROLLED creator's blocks while still admitting the enrolled participants', with all three anti-vacuity guards live: the rule finalized something, an enrolled participant WAS admitted, and the attacker IS interned by `build_wire::next_extra` so the refusal cannot be a HashMap miss
